title: Freezing Mark Guide — Mark Spread, Freeze Buildup and Hunter's Mark
summary: Freezing Mark is a Mark skill: you apply a freeze mark to an enemy, the marked enemy takes increased Freeze Buildup, and when it is killed or critically hit the mark spreads to nearby enemies. This guide explains how the mark is applied, what triggers the spread, how it differs from Sniper's Mark / Overwhelming Mark, why it naturally serves Frost builds, and the common 'mark won't spread / won't freeze' causes.
description: Freezing Mark deep guide: mark application and spread mechanic, freeze buildup bonus, comparison with other marks, recommended crit / cold supports, Ice Shot / Herald of Ice synergy, mark-won't-spread and freeze-fail causes with direct answers, video timestamps and real community questions.
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial

sections.title: Overview: One Mark, a Whole Freeze
paragraphs: Freezing Mark is a Mark skill: you apply a freeze mark to a single enemy. The marked enemy takes increased Freeze Buildup, so it freezes more easily; crucially, when that marked enemy is killed or critically hit, the mark automatically spreads to a nearby enemy — creating a 'kill one, freeze a pack' snowball.

Its role is not direct damage but an 'amplifier + crowd control' tool: a low-cost mark converts into multiplied freeze efficiency and group freezing. For builds that rely on freeze-trigger, shatter or freeze-control, it is the bridge that turns single-target control into area control.

This is why it fits naturally with Ice Shot / Herald of Ice frost systems: frost bow builds already spread chill and shatter, and Freezing Mark makes key targets (and the trash around them) freeze faster, so shatter and freeze-trigger payoffs are maxed.
bullets: Essence: single-target mark, raises target Freeze Buildup, spreads on kill / crit.
Role: amplifier + CC, deals no direct damage.
Mechanic: kill one → spread → freeze a pack, snowball.
Natural partners: Ice Shot / Herald of Ice frost systems.

sections.title: Mechanics: How the Mark Applies and Spreads
paragraphs: Application: you use Freezing Mark on an enemy and it carries the freeze mark. The mark itself deals no damage, but the target's received Freeze Buildup is raised — enemies that barely crossed the freeze threshold before now freeze more easily.

Spread condition: when the marked enemy is killed, or takes a critical hit, the mark jumps to a nearby enemy. This means 'pop the marked one → it spreads to the neighbor → that neighbor also becomes a high-buildup target → kill it to keep spreading' chains. Crit-triggered spread lets you sustain the snowball without needing kills, which is especially useful in high-HP boss phases.

Single-mark limit: usually you can have only one enemy as the 'primary mark' enjoying maximum bonus at a time (similar to the single-entry rule of curses). But spread secondary targets also inherit the freeze-buildup bonus, so the real payoff covers an area. Don't assume you can stack multiple independent marks.
bullets: Mark raises the target's Freeze Buildup, freezing it sooner.
Kill or crit triggers spread, jumping to a nearby enemy.
Crit spread sustains the snowball without kills (useful on bosses).
Usually one primary mark at a time; spread targets inherit the bonus.

sections.title: Role in Builds
paragraphs: CC core of Ice Shot Deadeye: the frost bow uses Ice Shot to spread chill and shatter, while Freezing Mark makes key targets and surrounding trash freeze faster, amplifying shatter and freeze-trigger payoffs. With Herald of Ice's shatter burst it closes the loop 'mark → freeze → shatter clear'.
Crit spread in boss phases: a high-HP boss can't be 'killed to spread', but crit spread keeps throwing the mark onto trash that spawns near the boss or relevant targets, sustaining CC.

Relation to freeze-trigger / shatter builds: any build relying on Freeze to trigger (e.g. Cast on Elemental Ailment's freeze route) or on shatter to clear directly benefits from Freezing Mark's faster freezing.
bullets: Ice Shot Deadeye: mark → freeze → shatter-clear loop.
Boss phases: sustain CC via crit spread, no kill needed.
Serves freeze-trigger / shatter builds; faster freeze = direct gain.

sections.title: Common Mistakes: No Spread / No Freeze
paragraphs: Mark won't spread: you applied it but neither killed nor crit the target, so spread never triggers. Direct answer: land a crit on the marked target, or kill it first, and the mark jumps to a neighbor.

Won't freeze: the mark only raises Freeze Buildup, not a guaranteed freeze — if your cold damage is too low, or the target is freeze-immune, the mark can't save it. Direct answer: confirm your cold damage fills the freeze threshold and the target isn't freeze-immune.

Assuming multiple independent marks: usually only one primary mark at a time. Direct answer: reserve the mark for the current key target and rely on spread for the rest, instead of trying to mark every mob.

Mark breaks your rotation: Freezing Mark is an extra action; spamming it disrupts your main attack rhythm. Direct answer: fold the mark into your rotation (mark elites, then focus-fire) rather than mindless clicking.
bullets: Direct answer: crit or kill the marked target to trigger spread.
Issue: marked but still won't freeze.
Direct answer: mark only adds buildup; low cold / immunity still no freeze.
Issue: trying to mark every mob.
Direct answer: one primary mark, spread covers the rest.

items.question: Does Freezing Mark deal damage directly?
answer: No. It is a mark / CC tool and deals no direct damage.
Its value is raising the target's Freeze Buildup and spreading on kill / crit.

items.question: What exactly triggers the spread?
answer: When the marked enemy is killed, or takes a critical hit, the mark jumps to a nearby enemy.
Crit-triggered spread sustains the snowball without kills, very useful in boss phases.

items.question: Why won't it freeze even after marking?
answer: The mark only raises Freeze Buildup, not a guaranteed freeze; low cold damage or freeze immunity still no freeze.
Direct answer: confirm cold damage fills the threshold and the target isn't immune.
